assumptions: The set is performed to one side at a time, but both arms and both legs do the same work, so laterality is bilateral.
The direction of rotation changes only which side the spinal rotators work, and spinal actions count on both sides, so a single definition is enough.
Elbows stay extended and the arms stay fixed relative to the torso, so no elbow or shoulder joint action is listed. Shoulder and elbow work is credited through stabilization demands.
The trunk rotation is the primary mover. Hip extension to hold the elevated hips is an assist action.
The feet are planted on the floor and the hands hold the cable handle, so the kinetic chain is treated as closed.
The cable load is held in the hands, so grip and wrist stability apply.
classification_reasons: The exercise is a supine stability-ball trunk rotation resisted by a cable. Both hands hold the handle with the arms extended over the chest, and the trunk rotates away from the pulley.
The movement is a trunk rotation with a held bridge position and fixed arms. The schema can represent this with lumbar_spine/rotation and a hip extension assist.
The images match the text: frame 1 shows the arms extended over the chest and frame 2 shows the torso and arms rotated to the side while the feet stay planted.

instructions: Connect a standard handle attachment, and position the cable to a middle pulley position.
Lie on a stability ball perpendicular to the cable and grab the handle with one hand. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
Grab the handle with both hands and fully extend your arms above your chest. You hands should be directly in-line with the pulley. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
Keep your hips elevated and abs engaged. Rotate your torso away from the pulley for a full-quarter rotation. Your body should be flat from head to knees.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner reset to the starting position. You should still have side tension on the cable in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
